content: Mermaid diagrams in the docs vault must render in OBSIDIAN, which is STRICTER than @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli — validating with the CLI alone is insufficient (it passed while Obsidian broke, twice). Two Obsidian gotchas: (1) SUBGRAPH TITLES must be SHORT single-line phrases — a long/parenthetical title (e.g. 'ACCUMULATORS · the loop's memory (read at ①, written at ③④)') WRAPS and clips behind the first child node; keep titles to one or two words + at most one '·' qualifier, and move the detail to an italic caption line ABOVE the ```mermaid block. (2) Nested-subgraph 'direction LR' overrides are IGNORED by Obsidian — don't rely on them; design the layout for the renderer's default vertical (TB) flow instead of fighting it. Both the methodology loop diagram and the README architecture diagram live in the repo; when editing either, render AND eyeball, and prefer short titles + TB flow. The mermaid-cli render is a syntax check, NOT a fidelity check for Obsidian.

title: The AI-assisted workflow IS loop engineering (two nested loops + two accumulators)
rationale: Reframing settled 2026-07-13. The plan->decompose->implement->review 'lifecycle' is not a pipeline — it is one iteration of an ENGINEERED LOOP whose defining feature is that each pass leaves artifacts that make the next pass better. TWO nested loops at two timescales: (1) INNER loop (per-slice, hours) = the per-ticket prime->build->test->*architecture-review+refactor->e2e->commit, where the * gate is self-correction (unit-green triggers review-and-refactor BEFORE heavier validation) + fix-until-green with the >=3-attempts bounded blocked-exit; (2) OUTER loop (across slices, weeks) = the retrospective-into-planning cycle. TWO ACCUMULATORS make it compound rather than evaporate: MULCH = procedural/experiential memory (ml prime before, ml record after; the autonomous-runs domain literally feeds run-outcomes back into the next slice's phase-1 planning — B4-too-big mx-76cf08 -> the slice-sizing gate is that loop having fired once); the OBSIDIAN VAULT = declarative/decisional memory (immutable ADRs, living guides, STATUS notes, review notes, QA records — the loop's state store that phase-1 reads). HONEST CAVEAT: the loop is human-gated at the outer boundary (maintainer runs /decompose, kicks off the run, does phase-4, decides merges) — a loop with a human closing it each turn, NOT a fully-autonomous self-improving flywheel (that is the Warren AI-Software-Factory direction). For a portfolio/consulting artifact that auditability is a FEATURE. CONSEQUENCE: docs/methodology/AI-ENGINEERING-METHODOLOGY.md should LEAD with the loop frame (inner+outer loops, Mulch+vault accumulators), with the 4-phase lifecycle as one iteration — stronger + more honest than the pipeline framing. Upstream credits: Mulch (Jaymin West), grill-me (Matt Pocock), Anthropic dynamic-workflows/harness patterns.

title: Sub-agents scout and validate; the implementer implements (autonomous-run delegation policy)
rationale: Decided with the maintainer 2026-06-11 (Phase 5.95 planning), pinned in AUTONOMOUS-IMPLEMENTATION-FLOW.md (the section-4 template line + a section-7 rationale bullet + an operator-note bullet). The per-ticket implementation stays in the main loop: across 8 shipped runs the failure modes were unpinned design semantics and rig gotchas, never context exhaustion, while cross-ticket continuity (T1 micro-decisions shaping later tickets) is what keeps a run coherent; per-ticket sub-agents re-read the whole package + re-prime Mulch each time (similar token cost) and drift at every seam. ALLOWED delegation: read-only scouting fan-outs (e.g. 'which collections assert list bodies') and log-noisy validation (run newman/build, return only the failure summary). Context pressure is handled by stopping at a checkpoint and resuming in a FRESH SESSION - the ticket status table + STATUS-0N notes are a complete handoff (the method is doc-first so the window is cache, not the source of truth).

title: Phase 7 reordered (2026-07-06): baseline full security review NOW (7.0.5), 7.4 re-scoped to delta + publish checklist, load-test scope pinned
rationale: Decided with the maintainer after PR #52. (1) Full security review moved BEFORE the user-directory slice: every prior deep-review was diff-scoped, so B4 tenant isolation + 6.7 control plane + PR-#52 self-service UI were never reviewed as ONE attack surface — and the control plane (team mgmt, custom-role editor, self-service create) is the classic privilege-escalation surface; findings feed the user-directory grill-me (directory search = enumeration/PII surface); that slice introduces a Keycloak ADMIN credential, so enter it from a verified baseline. (2) 7.4 pre-publish pass re-scoped to DELTA since the baseline + publish checklist (repo-history secret scan, dependency CVE audit, zero-config fail-safety, signing/supply chain) — 7.3 perf tweaks are the most security-sensitive remaining changes (decision caching = stale-authorization hazard; breaker/retry tuning changes fail-closed timing). (3) Load testing stays pre-publish (7.2), scope pinned: four library hot paths through the example services — gate overhead delta vs unguarded (p50/95/99 headline), partial-eval list path + OPA compile ceiling, enrichment multiplier (_actions fan-out/batching bound), resilience under fault (OPA slow/down, breaker cycle, B2 supplier edge) — plus the cross-service amplification ratio (1 catalog request -> N user-mgmt/OPA calls; request caches must bound it). OUT: demo UI, Keycloak login throughput, APISIX tuning. Reuse the Docker rig + B3 fault injector; tooling picked at decompose. Deliverable: PERFORMANCE.md.

title: Slice 5.5-B (hierarchy-aware list filter): the 6 settled forks + ADR 0010
rationale: Planning grilled the list-specific forks ADR 0008 deferred; all pinned in ADR 0010 (the list fork is 0010, not 0009 — 0009 was taken by tag-requirement-subject-side). The 6 decisions: (1) ROOT-ONLY subtree roots — subtreeSpec = whole governing-root subtree iff the root-resolved role inheritably grants the verb, else empty; mid-tree per-node grants are Phase 8; reuses the existing root role lookup, no new 'which nodes' search. (2) SEAM = a new SubtreeSpecResolver (spring-data, owns root-resolution + inheritable gate + calls subtreeOf) feeding an ADDITIVE 4-arg AbacQueryService.findAuthorized(repo,scope,ctx,subtreeSpec) that owns scope.and(tagResidual.or(subtreeSpec)).and(notDenied); 3-arg PRESERVED byte-compatible (delegates subtreeSpec=null); AbacQueryService gains NO resolver dep on the composition path (receives a ready Specification). (3) notDenied = SQL mirror of the shipped leaf deny abac_deny==true -> the SQL predicate `abac_deny IS DISTINCT FROM true` over tags JSONB, AND-ed OUTSIDE the OR (folding it inside lets the subtree branch re-admit a denied row); absent tag -> not denied (matches Rego); future non-scalar deny -> route to allowlist batch (documented, not built). (4) NEW additive SPI method AncestorResolver.subtreeOf(rootType,rootId) -> Specification (NOT Set<id>, to keep the ltree pushdown + strategy behind the SPI): ltree -> path <@ <root-label> SQL pushdown (id set never materialized); CTE -> id IN (descendants) downward walk BOUNDED by maxDepth, FAIL-CLOSED to always-false on breach/cycle/error. (5) The !fullySupported allowlist BATCH path becomes hierarchy-aware: batchFilter/withResource build per-row AbacContext WITH the row's ancestor chain (4-arg Resource) so allowAll decides each row by the same Rego final_allow as the single-GET; subtreeSpec applies to the PURE-SQL path ONLY; adds an AncestorResolver dep to the batch path (constructor change = build-breaker, update all sites same commit); cheap (ltree path already loaded). (6) ONE slice, 6 tickets (T1 subtreeOf SPI+both impls+ITs; T2 SubtreeSpecResolver; T3 4-arg overload+notDenied+batch; T4 IT no-leak+re-parent-on-list; T5 starter+example adoption; T6 e2e+docs), not split — the widening + the deny narrowing are one atomic correctness unit. FAIL-CLOSED everywhere: failed subtree resolution -> narrower tag-only (never wider); subtreeSpec OR-ed INSIDE scope.and (never escapes scope); opa-abac-core NOT touched; residual/operator-set/RoleDefinition unchanged. The recurring autonomous-run pause class (a fail-open/contract semantic left unpinned) is pre-empted: root-only, notDenied-outside-OR, batch-carries-ancestors, subtreeOf-fail-closed are all pinned in advance.

content: Structural decisions get an ADR as part of decomposition — written UP FRONT, not after. ADRs live in docs/architecture/adr/NNNN-short-title.md (lightly-MADR: Status / Context / Decision / Considered options WITH why-rejected / Consequences) with an index README. A decision is 'structural' (=> needs an ADR) when it would be expensive to reverse or surprising to a future reader: a schema/authority shape, a module/service boundary, where a check is evaluated (app vs Rego/policy), an additive-vs-breaking choice, or a deliberate 'we did NOT do X' with real alternatives weighed. Routine choices (naming, file layout, test lib) do NOT need one. WHY up front: a feature's 00-DESIGN/01-DECOMPOSITION are LIVING docs that get rewritten and git-mv'd to implemented/ on ship, so rationale buried there drifts; an ADR is IMMUTABLE — it pins the decision + rejected alternatives at a point in time and is SUPERSEDED (never edited) by a later ADR (flip the old status to 'Superseded by [[NNNN-...]]'). Heuristic: if you catch yourself writing a 'considered & rejected' list worth keeping, that's an ADR. The planning step is now: decomposition surfaces a fork -> write/update the ADR -> link it from 00-DESIGN. (Records 0001-0004 for the user-management entity graph / team-target / role-defs / tag dictionary were backfilled retroactively; going forward the ADR is authored with the decomposition.)

title: User-directory slice: 2-way split; Slice 2 = pure-search UserDirectory port + optional Keycloak-admin module (grill-me settled 2026-07-06)
rationale: Grilled the Phase-7 user-directory plan-of-record into TWO slices (§2a). SLICE 1 (separate, self-evident): server-side listAll*-killer filters — ?subject on /users, ?targetType/?targetId on /teams, produces/Accept spec fix, bootstrap displayName upsert; one deployable, no external dep, ~4 tickets. SLICE 2 (designed here): the Keycloak-admin UserDirectory port. 8 pinned decisions: (1) split along feature-vs-filters. (2) PURE SEARCH read-model — provisioning explicitly OUT of scope (SPA provisions on select via existing POST /users); the SPI is search-only so consumers can implement provisioning differently. (3) Port UserDirectory.search(String query,int limit)->List<DirectoryUser> + DirectoryUser(subject,displayName) record + NoOpUserDirectory default in opa-abac-spring-security (mirrors ResourceOwnershipResolver); Keycloak impl in its OWN optional module (opa-abac-keycloak-directory) auto-wired like Resilience4j (@ConditionalOnClass+@ConditionalOnProperty, NoOp fallback -> lean-starter preserved). (4) Keycloak auth = dedicated catalog-directory confidential client, serviceAccountsEnabled, client_credentials grant, granted ONLY realm-management->view-users on catalog-demo (least privilege, no human credential, separate trust role from catalog-gateway). (5) GET /api/v1/users/search?q=&limit= on the user-service UserApi (spec-first), bearer-only; response a BOUNDED PLAIN LIST {items:[{subject,displayName}],limit} NOT a fake Page envelope. (6) keycloak:8888 in-network URL is a PRIVATE impl/config detail of the module — port+endpoint stay URL-agnostic (encapsulation); ADR notes KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN_URL=localhost:28888 is a console-rewrite red herring, not the REST path. (7) authz: bearer-only (consistent w/ ungated GET /users), disclosure TYPE-BOUNDED to {subject,displayName} in the DTO so no impl can widen it; the real gate stays on team:add-member; documented as a deliberate decision (not an ungated-enumeration finding). (8) fail-closed: 7 edges pinned — unreachable/timeout/5xx->[], grant-fail->[]+WARN, blank q->[] WITHOUT calling Keycloak, limit clamped default 20 hard-max 50, null username->fall back to subject, module-off->NoOp []; BINARY port (empty-or-results), outage vs genuine-empty distinguishable ONLY in logs — SPA renders both identically as a deliberate NO-ORACLE security property (never leak backend state/realm size to UI). §2a: Slice 2 passes as ONE purely-additive slice (trips (b) multi-deployable + borderline (c) ticket count, but CLEAN on the dangerous (a) remove-and-replace and (d) unenumerable-consumers); sequenced BACKEND-FIRST (newman-provable before SPA rewrite); SPA-split (2a/2b) held in reserve if decomposition >~6 tickets. NET-NEW: zero existing Keycloak-admin code in the repo; KC 26.3.2, realm catalog-demo.

title: Phase 5 data-filtering planned: partial-eval (compile→DNF residual→JPA Specification) + batch, fail-closed, abstract OpaClient methods
rationale: Phase 5 (the advanced-library slice) is planned+decomposed in docs/to-do/planning/DATA-FILTERING/ (full package: index, 00-DESIGN, 01-DECOMPOSITION T1-T7, AUTONOMOUS-IMPLEMENTATION-PROMPT, 10-QA, 7 STATUS stubs) mirroring the four shipped slices 1:1. SCOPE (confirmed w/ maintainer): partial-eval + batch BOTH, NOT hierarchical ancestor-walk (that filters by ancestors; this slice filters by the row's OWN tags — the load-then-check CategoryAuthorizer stub stays). KEY DECISIONS: (1) Two ADDITIVE OpaClient methods — compile(AbacContext)->PartialResult via OPA Compile API (POST /v1/compile, query 'data/<type>/filter == true', unknowns=['input.resource'], resource OMITTED from input) and allowAll(List<AbacContext>)->List<Boolean> via a per-type 'bulk' rule. Make them ABSTRACT, not default methods, so a custom OpaClient cannot silently inherit a fail-OPEN filter. allow() + the @OpaPreAuthorize path stay byte-for-byte unchanged. (2) Neutral residual model in core (Spring-free): PartialResult{decision ALLOW_ALL|DENY_ALL|CONDITIONAL, List<Conjunction>} = DNF (OR-of-ANDs); Condition{path, Operator EQ|NEQ|IN|CONTAINS, value}. Mapping: compile result absent/{}->ALLOW_ALL; result.queries==[]->DENY_ALL; non-empty->CONDITIONAL. (3) ResidualSpecificationFactory in spring-data translates residual->Specification<T> over the tags JSONB (GIN-indexed since domain-model slice): EQ/IN via jsonb_extract_path_text(tags,'k'); CONTAINS (array tag) via the ? existence op jsonb_exists(tags->'k','v') — mirrors the TAG-DICTIONARY resource_tag_values scalar-vs-array normalize (mx-666644); intrinsic path (e.g. categoryId)->root.get(). ALLOW_ALL->no predicate; DENY_ALL->cb.disjunction() (always false). Postgres-only dialect (seam noted, second dialect not built). (4) FAIL-CLOSED is the load-bearing invariant: compile error->DENY_ALL (empty page); batch error->all-false; an UNSUPPORTED residual (operator outside the closed set / a non-input.resource ref) -> DENY_ALL, or with allowlistFallback=on -> exact batch re-check over a recognized-conjunct pre-filter. NEVER 'return everything' on error. The closed small operator set is deliberate (narrow-but-correct > wide-but-wrong: a mistranslated predicate = a silent data leak). (5) Three-layer separation: Compile-API+DNF in core, JSONB->Criteria in spring-data, the rego 'filter'/'bulk' entrypoints in policy. The differentiator (mx-15ee3e): the one comparable OSS project opa-data-filter is unmaintained. Lead-in still distinct from Phase-7 ReBAC-in-Rego (mx-723b5c). Planning branch: feature/void3110/plan-data-filtering.

title: Roadmap expanded: action enrichment = Phase 6 (affordance map via response advice + action registry + x-implements DTO marker); two ADRs pinned (0005 partial-eval, 0006 three-layer)
rationale: Roadmap grown along two routes (maintainer ask): tech topics + user stories, anchored by ADRs. KEY ADDITIONS: (1) ACTION ENRICHMENT as a new Phase 6 (bumps publish 6->7, ReBAC 7->8), planning note docs/to-do/planning/ACTION-ENRICHMENT (direction set, not yet decomposed; sequenced after Phase 5 because it is the FIRST consumer of the Phase-5 batch primitive OpaClient.allowAll). Enrichment = attach a {action:allowed} affordance map to a returned resource/page so a UI renders the right buttons. It is AFFORDANCE, NOT enforcement (enforcement = ADR 0006 three layers). Decided shape: a response decorator/ResponseBodyAdvice (automatic, not per-endpoint boilerplate); action source = a per-resource-type ACTION REGISTRY (generalizes the source platform's ActionName enum + ResourceTypeActions; doubles as a validation allowlist; superior to role-permissions-only because it can report delete:false for an ungranted verb). (2) THE KEY MECHANISM for fitting enrichment to OpenAPI codegen: stamp resource DTOs with an x-implements vendor extension so the org.openapi.generator 'spring' generator makes the generated POJO implement a library marker interface (e.g. Enrichable) — confirmed against the source platform's external-credentials DTO which stamps java.lang.AutoCloseable via 'x-implements: [java.lang.AutoCloseable]' + 'x-closeable: true'. The advice detects Enrichable returns, batch-evals, injects _actions. App opts in with ONE x-implements line in its spec — no DTO hand-editing/post-processing. Open Q held for Phase-6 planning: the envelope shape (inline _actions vs a wrapping Authorized<T>). (3) USER STORIES route: docs/to-do/planning/USER-STORIES.md — the PRODUCT lens over the tech roadmap; personas (viewer/editor/owner-admin/super-admin/integrator) + epics A-F each tagged to its delivering phase (A=P3 enforcement, B=P4 team roles, C=P4.5 tags, D=P5 list filtering, E=P6 enrichment, F=P7 publish). (4) ADRs authored UP FRONT per our own convention (mx — the ADR-in-decomposition convention): 0005 partial-eval->JPA Specification (pins the DATA-FILTERING fork: compile API->DNF residual->Specification over tags JSONB, fail-closed, abstract-not-default OpaClient methods), 0006 the three-layer enforcement model (gateway coarse -> app @OpaPreAuthorize/load-then-check -> DB partial-eval; THE PRINCIPLE: the app NEVER trusts the gateway, re-decides every single-resource return against the loaded resource to stop horizontal privilege escalation on a guessed ID — the gateway is defense-in-depth, not the decision). 0005/0006 are the first ADRs written up-front (0001-0004 were retroactive). Action-enrichment ADR PENDING (written with its decomposition). Branch: feature/void3110/plan-data-filtering (continuation).

description: The per-ticket workflow runs a clean-room/build check with 'git add -A' (or 'git add -A' to stage a diff for scanning) and ALSO records Mulch with 'ml record … && ml sync'. ml sync stages and commits whatever it considers part of the expertise update — but in practice it commits EVERYTHING currently staged, not just .mulch/. So a 'mulch: update expertise' commit silently swept in the ticket's source/docs/a git-mv folder rename three separate times this run, violating the hard rule that Mulch sync commits must touch .mulch/ ONLY (and mixing code into a commit titled 'mulch: …').
resolution: Before 'ml sync', ensure the index contains ONLY .mulch/ — run 'git restore --staged .' (unstage everything) then either let ml sync stage .mulch itself, or 'git add .mulch/' explicitly. If a mixed 'mulch: …' commit already happened, recover with: git reset --soft HEAD~1; git restore --staged .; git add .mulch/; git commit -m 'mulch: …'; then git add <the ticket's real paths> and commit the source separately. Order the per-ticket steps so the clean-room scan uses 'git add -A' + 'git diff --cached' + 'git restore --staged .' (leaving a CLEAN index) BEFORE doing the Mulch record/sync, so ml sync can't capture staged source.

description: verify-package.sh's clean-room scan (scripts/planning/verify-package.sh [3]) runs grep -rnEi (CASE-INSENSITIVE) with a GENERIC pattern that includes '/Users/[a-z]' (to catch leaked mac home-dir paths like /Users/<name>). Case-insensitively this ALSO matches the public REST path fragment '/users/<lowercase-letter>' — so a decomposition package that writes a literal API path like '/users/search' or '/users/by-subject' trips a FALSE-POSITIVE clean-room violation and the gate fails. Shipped packages passed only because their user/team paths are always '/users/{id}' or '/teams/{teamId}' — the char after the collection is '{', not [a-z], so no match. Hit while decomposing DIRECTORY-QUERY-FILTERS (Slice 1 of user-directory).
resolution: Reword the prose so the collection segment is NOT immediately followed by a lowercase letter: write 'a search endpoint under /api/v1/users' or 'a by-subject sub-path under /api/v1/users' instead of the bare '/users/search' / '/users/by-subject/{sub}'. The path is still clear; the /users/<lower> literal is avoided. (Do NOT weaken the GENERIC pattern — /Users/[a-z] earns its keep catching real home-dir leaks; the case-insensitive collision is the price.) Confirmed: after rewording, verify-package.sh DIRECTORY-QUERY-FILTERS => PACKAGE OK.

title: Phase 9 (agent tool-call authz): the 8 settled forks (grill-me 2026-07-27)
rationale: Grilled with the maintainer 2026-07-27; full design brief + re-verification in the vault note Agent-Tool-Call-Authorization-Direction.md. SETTLED: (1) scope fence ABOVE the validated token — transport/OAuth OUT (mcp-security's job; principal = validated token's sub/claims), tool+argument ABAC IN, RAG = Phase-10 lane; PREREQ: diff FINAL vs RC on authz/tools sections when the 2026-07-28 spec text publishes. (2) PEP legs: server-side @McpTool AuthorizationManager-style gate FIRST (corp-shape mirror), host-side ToolCallingManager decorator second; engine core leg-agnostic; identity rides ToolContext never ThreadLocals. (3) identity: RFC 8693 act semantics canonical, normalized by a DelegationChainExtractor SPI; demo tier = plain custom claim on stock Keycloak; Keycloak 26.8 native-act showcase documented, rig NOT pinned to nightly. (4) agent model: principal role = ceiling (existing RoleDefinitionSupplier unchanged) ∩ agent capability profile that only narrows (new AgentCapabilitySupplier, same tri-state doctrine, turn-scoped memo); intersection computed in Rego; NO standing agent grants; agents in UserDirectory as read-model only. (5) input schema: two-layer (tool-gate powers roster/tools-list filtering via allowAll; target-gate feeds EXISTING per-type policies UNCHANGED with the pre-narrowed role_definition); additive input.subject.actor/chain; published versioned input-schema spec = the standard-setting deliverable. (5b) topology: two-step short-circuit (tool-gate always; resolve+target-gate only on allow AND domain-addressing tool); deny = structured advisory tool-error naming the layer, 403 only when scope-expressible. (6) packaging: example-first in a new example-mcp-server over the catalog domain; extract OPTIONAL module opa-abac-agent (keycloak-directory packaging template) as the slice EXIT criterion; publication rides the next release train. (residual 8) roster = call-time-only enforcement in v1, listChanged documented follow-up. (residual 10) tools declare action/category/tags statically; ToolCallClassifier SPI ships contract-only (most-restrictive-on-ambiguity), no impl in v1. PINNED (not forks): fail-closed tri-state on every new edge, per-layer kill-switches, HITL OUT of v1, smallest-honest-demo = scripted no-LLM MCP client, module extraction = exit not entry.

title: Phase 9 decomposition: enforcement-by-composition (no role propagation) — the fork decomposition surfaced
rationale: Decomposing AGENT-TOOL-AUTHZ (2026-07-28) surfaced a structural fork the grill had not reached: once the MCP server's tools proxy the catalog REST API, how does the AGENT's narrowing reach the target-gate? The grill had said 'pass a pre-narrowed role_definition' — but that means the catalog service TRUSTING a role asserted by its caller, exactly the caller-supplied-authority shape slice B4 removed. RESOLVED (maintainer, ADR 0028): TWO-LAYER ENFORCEMENT BY COMPOSITION, no propagation. The tool-gate (MCP server) is the sole home of agent narrowing; the catalog independently enforces the principal ceiling with policies literally untouched; net effect = the intersection, provably, with NOTHING asserted downstream (the caller's bearer is forwarded byte-for-byte, no role/capability/acting-as header). Honest cost recorded in the ADR: the per-type policies do not see the actor this slice; a tool needing agent-aware row filtering would need a later propagation design with a real trust boundary. GENERAL LESSON (reusable): when an agent/proxy layer sits in front of a service that already enforces, prefer composing two independent enforcement points over propagating a computed decision — propagation needs a trust boundary the composition does not. Also settled at decompose time: tools proxy the existing REST API (no shared DB, no duplicated enforcement, no read-before-gate hop); package = 6 tickets, sizing gate passes because the slice is purely additive (no shared mechanism changed, one new deployable); module extraction (opa-abac-agent) is the slice EXIT criterion, not ticket 1.

name: Recurring pause classes become GATES, not louder advice: the decompose two-gate model (mechanical citation/link checks + adversarial seam/semantics/consistency fan-out)
description: Established 2026-07-31 after the AGENT-TOOL-AUTHZ run paused twice on one root cause. THE RULE: when a run-retrospective names a pause class twice, mechanize it; prose in a guide degrades silently, a scripted or agentic gate does not. LEDGER (class -> gate): blast-radius-unenumerable -> the slice-sizing gate; fail-open/contract semantic unpinned -> the unpinned-semantics critic; a third-party seam named from a mental model -> the verify-the-artifact ticket rule + seam-existence auditors. THE TWO GATES, neither substituting for the other: (1) MECHANICAL verify-package.sh + scripts/planning/check-citations.py - files/frontmatter/clean-room/slots/prompt-skeleton/ticket-STATUS parity PLUS acceptance-citation cross-reference (every cited U*/I*/E* exists AND the QA doc assigns it to the citing ticket, both directions, ranges expanded) PLUS wikilink resolution; (2) ADVERSARIAL .claude/skills/decompose/decompose-validation-workflow.js - 4 angles (library seams via javap against the Gradle-cache jar / internal+policy+config+command seams / unpinned-semantics critic primed on autonomous-runs / cross-doc consistency incl. whether the PROMPT can even express every failure class the design defines), each finding attacked 4 ways before it is reported, ranked run-stopper|contradiction|nit. EVIDENCE IT WORKS: first mechanical run on a package that had passed every prior gate found 17 broken citations + 35 uncited QA cases (incl. a phantom P1-P10 series and the entire U18-U30 rego suite); the adversarial run found 19 confirmed / 24 refuted, its headline being that OpaClient.allowAll is contractually total so the roster degradation trigger could never fire - a defect in text written the previous day and already reviewed by two ad-hoc auditors. CALIBRATION RULE: run both gates against an ALREADY-SHIPPED package during instantiation; a gate reporting nothing on real input is untested, not clean. WORKFLOW-SCRIPT TRAP found the same day: args can arrive JSON-ENCODED, so args.slice silently resolves to String.prototype.slice and every agent gets a nonsense path - parse defensively and log() the resolved scope.

title: Defer the opa-abac-agent extraction to the SECOND consumer, not to an SDK version
rationale: Decided 2026-08-01, immediately after Phase 9 merged (PR #95). The slice's stated exit criterion was 'extract a reusable opa-abac-agent module'; the question raised was whether to do it now or wait for Spring AI / MCP java-sdk 2.1. ANSWER: neither trigger — wait for the second consumer. MEASURED, not assumed: all 14 MCP-SDK/Spring-AI imports in example-mcp-server sit in FOUR classes (~380 LOC: RosterFilterInstaller, ToolCallGate, ToolRosterFilter, ToolAuthorizationConfiguration), while the ~800-LOC kernel — the whole identity/ package, ToolCallAuthorizer, TypeLevelRoleDefinitionSupplier, the registry, the decision/error types — has ZERO. So 'wait for Spring AI' only ever argued about the adapter, and the adapter is already designed to be deleted when java-sdk #578 ships (open, milestone 2.1.0). THE REAL BLOCKER IS N=1, and three seams say so: (a) TypeLevelRoleDefinitionSupplier hard-codes THIS demo's /internal/governed-targets + /internal/effective-roles, had zero tests until the deep review, and carried a defect only the rig found; (b) ConfigAgentCapabilitySupplier is the only capability source and QA case I6 (the tri-state over a real HTTP edge) was WAIVED as unimplementable — the contract most likely to be reshaped by a real consumer has never met one; (c) the gate-off semantics were found incoherent by the deep review 24h earlier. PLAN: port the pattern BY HAND into the next consumer with no library, let a different tool surface + role source + capability source pull the seams into shape, extract at N=2 following the in-repo precedent — UserDirectory became a port with opa-abac-keycloak-directory as its optional adapter only once it had a real impl AND a real consumer. DO NOW at zero API cost: freeze the CONTRACT not the Java (agent_tools.rego + the capability profile's JSON wire shape are the reusable ideas and are copyable files, already documented in the guide), and hide TypeLevelRoleDefinitionSupplier's HTTP specifics behind an interface INSIDE the example so the port boundary is discovered while still free to move. THE ASYMMETRY THAT SETTLED IT: waiting costs ~nothing (the example works; the reflective adapter is guarded by a startup failure + kill-switch; the pattern is documented), while extracting early means owning a PUBLISHED artifact compiled against SDK 2.0.0 internals exactly as 2.1 reshapes them — waiting converts a future compatibility problem into a future deletion. Stated bias: the decision was made by the same party that wrote the code, so 'how reusable is it' is not a neutral judgement; the disconfirming case is a time-boxed second consumer for whom copying ~1200 lines is worse than depending on a 0.x — in which case ship an honest 0.x with an 'API will move' note, never a 1.0 shaped by one example.

title: SUPERVISOR-STEP-UP phase ①: grounding the grill in the code overturned three of the research brief's recommended answers
rationale: The 2026-07-27 research pass produced a design that was right in shape but wrong in three specifics, each caught only by reading the shipped code BEFORE asking the fork. (1) 'env is operator-protected exactly like the abac_deny precedent' is not implementable: abac_deny is protected by NOT EXISTING in the tag dictionary (the sole assignment gate is 'does this key resolve to a definition'), but env must exist to be assignable and enum-validated. The obvious substitute, the existing is_system flag, is also wrong - the two seeded GLOBAL keys the entire demo assigns (sensitivity, region) are both is_system=true, where it means 'definition immutable through the API'. Overloading it would have broken the seed demo, the e2e matrix and the SPA tag editors. Resolution: a NEW additive operatorManaged boolean, carried through TagDefinitionView (which drops is_system today) and enforced in TagAssignmentService. (2) The proposed catalog:read / catalog:read-detail verb split is unnecessary: GET /catalogs/{id} is ALREADY metadata-only, so a catalog has no 'detail' to gate - its contents are literally the child endpoints. Dropping the split avoids touching the mirrored permission_categories.json in both service bundles. (3) CRITIC FIX 2's 'carry root attributes into child decision inputs by enriching ancestors' would have cost N entity loads: ParentRef is (type,id) only and NEITHER ancestor resolver loads entities (Ltree decodes path label strings, RecursiveCte walks parent links) - that is precisely the optimization those resolvers exist for. The governing root's id is in the PATH of every child endpoint, so one memoized fetch by id gives root_attributes with ParentRef and both resolvers untouched. Two forks the agenda did not even contain turned out to be the load-bearing ones: the member-AND-supervisor PRECEDENCE rule (membership wins => supervised := S \ M => the scopes are disjoint => the critic's fail-open becomes structurally impossible instead of a check that must be written correctly), and REACH (a report's CONTROL-capable memberships only, not any membership - otherwise one report's READER seat on an unrelated team silently widens their manager). Also settled: elevation attaches to the supervised PATH, not to the env tag globally, which keeps every existing persona and all 15 ROPC collections unchanged.

description: SUPERVISED-SCOPE decomposition (2026-08-01): the mechanical gate (verify-package.sh) went GREEN on a package carrying TWO run-stoppers, either of which would have wasted most of an autonomous run. Both were invisible to it by construction, because verify-package.sh checks SHAPE — files present, frontmatter, citations resolving, prompt skeleton intact, wikilinks — and neither defect was a shape defect. (1) The synthesized supervisor RoleDefinition was specified as permissions={"catalog":["view","list"]}. Since ADR 0007/0015 permissions[<type>] carries COARSE CATEGORY TOKENS (READ/WRITE/TAG/GRANT/CONTROL) that data.permission_categories expands into fine verbs; view/list are the EXPANSION of READ, not tokens, and an unrecognized token expands to the EMPTY set (the documented fail-closed empty-expansion for a pre-6.5 flat role). The role would therefore have granted NOTHING - catalog.allow false, the filter residual DENY_ALL, the supervised page silently empty - and the failure is invisible until the e2e, because the QA case as written (U14) asserted the same wrong Java shape. Docs, tests and code all agreed with each other and disagreed only with OPA. (2) The two-leg list was specified as leg1.or(leg2) handed to AbacQueryService.findAuthorized, but that method takes ONE AbacContext, compiles ONE residual from it, and composes scope.and(tagResidual.or(subtreeSpec)).and(notDenied()) - there is no overload taking two (scope, context) legs and no public method turning a role into a residual Specification, so the single residual would have been AND-ed over the whole union and narrowed the supervised rows by the membership role.
resolution: Never ship a package on the mechanical gate alone - run the adversarial validation workflow, which is what caught both (50 agents, 20 confirmed / 26 refuted; each run-stopper independently corroborated by 2-3 angles, which is the signal that separated them from the 26 refuted ones). Fixes: permissions={"catalog":["READ"]} with U14 restated to assert via opa eval that data.catalog.filter is true and data.category.allow is false under the role - NOT the Java shape alone, since a Java-only assertion passes on a role that grants nothing; and the two legs composed through the SHIPPED findAuthorized 4-arg overload with supervised ids riding the subtreeSpec slot (the ADR-0010 base-scope-widening idiom), yielding scope AND (residual_membership OR id-in-supervised) AND notDenied, plus a new QA case pinning the precondition that makes it correct (the supervisor role's residual is ALLOW_ALL because it grants READ with empty requiredTags). GENERALIZATION - the two defect classes the shape gate cannot see: (a) a VOCABULARY-LEVEL error, where a value is well-formed and plausible but belongs to the wrong layer of an expansion table, and (b) an API-SHAPE error, where a named method cannot express the composition the design assumes. Both are the flow guide's keystone lesson (a seam named from a mental model rather than checked against the artifact) applied to values and to composition rather than to method names. Cheap prophylactic for the next decomposition: for every literal that will be consumed by a policy or an expansion table, write the assertion against the CONSUMER (opa eval) and not against the producing Java object; and for every composition the design draws as pseudo-code, open the method it will call and confirm the parameter it maps onto exists.

description: A docs-package commit (8f50f7a, 2026-08-01) silently shipped WITHOUT the package files its message described. Cause: the staging command was 'git add <new-folder>/ <old-renamed-path> 2>/dev/null' - the second pathspec no longer existed (the folder had been git-mv'd earlier in the session), git add fails the ENTIRE invocation on any unmatched pathspec, and the 2>/dev/null swallowed the only evidence. A later git add of other files succeeded, so the commit was non-empty and looked plausible; git log printed the expected subject line and the omission surfaced only when a later git status showed the 'committed' files as untracked.
resolution: Two rules. (1) Never combine pathspecs in one git add when any of them might not exist - and never silence git add's stderr; a pathspec that fails the whole add plus a suppressed error message is a silent no-op that produces a plausible-looking commit. (2) After any commit whose message enumerates content, verify with 'git show --stat' that the enumerated files are actually in it - the subject line proves nothing. Fixed by follow-up commit b5da8ac (honest fix-up naming the cause), not by history rewrite - mulch sync commits had already landed on top.

name: Additive gate evolution: prove byte-identity by corpus-wide old-vs-new diff with the new block stripped
description: When a shared mechanical gate (verify-package.sh) gains a check [N], the additive guarantee is provable, not asserted: extract the OLD script from git (git show HEAD:path), run old and new across EVERY real package, assert (1) exit-code parity per package and (2) byte-identical output after awk-stripping exactly the new [N] block from the new output. Strip ONLY the block's own lines (header + indented result lines), never the surrounding blank line — a sloppy strip manufactures phantom diffs on all packages (measured 2026-08-01: 25 false BYTE-DIFFs from one eaten blank line). PARTS-PORT T1 ran this across 25 packages: 0 rc diffs, 0 byte diffs. Pairs with a calibration sweep (run the new sub-checker alone on the whole corpus and record the count) - a parser that has never seen real input is untested, not clean.

title: Parts-port T3: mode resolution is a mechanical contract over check-parts.py output, never a re-parse
rationale: The /autonomous-implement runner's three-mode resolution (single-session / ORCHESTRATOR / PART-RUNNER / contradiction-stop) is specified as a table keyed ONLY on check-parts.py's exit code + first summary line + the 'part N' argument. This keeps the single-validation-authority invariant airtight (the skill and any drill consume the checker's validated echo - even the PART-RUNNER's ticket range comes from the summary line, never from re-reading 00-DESIGN.md) and makes the E1 mode drill a 40-line script that mirrors the skill's table verbatim instead of a 4x live skill invocation. General shape: when a skill's branching must be testable, define the branch condition as a pure function of one tool's machine output and drill THAT.

description: SYMPTOM (reproduced live, PARTS-PORT T4 drill E4c): grepping for a fixed markdown marker containing '**' and '()' as a raw ERE - grep -E '^**ESCALATION (cross-part):**' - does not match-nothing, it ERRORS (exit 2, repetition-operator operand invalid). Any consumer testing truthiness (if grep ...; then) reads exit 2 exactly like exit 1 'absent' - a silent fail-open on whatever channel the marker carries (here: the cross-part escalation channel of the parts orchestrator).
resolution: Escape every ERE metacharacter in the fixed string and DISTINGUISH the three exit classes, never truthiness: 0=found->HALT, 1=absent->proceed, >=2=the CHECK failed->HALT too. Anchor to the start of a line's content with a prefix-character allowlist ([[:space:]>*+-]*) so mid-sentence prose and backticked documentation mentions cannot match (false HALTs) while bullets and quotes still do. Same discipline for ANY marker-file/sentinel-line check, not just these two markers.

description: SYMPTOM (measured 2026-08-01): a multi-agent validation workflow returned counts {confirmed:0, refuted:0, runStoppers:0} — which reads exactly like a clean pass — while 37 of its 41 agents had ERRORED on a session/usage limit, including EVERY verification (refutation) agent. The audit agents had actually returned 37 candidate findings, one a ground-truth-proven run-stopper; because verification never ran, none were promoted into the counts. A caller that reads only the counts field ships a package the gate never cleared. Same failure shape as the raw-grep-errors-vs-absent trap (mx-…): an ERRORED check is not an ABSENT result.
resolution: Never read a workflow's counts without reading its agent-error tally in the same breath: agents_error>0 with confirmed==0 means NOT-RUN, never CLEAN — treat it as a failed gate and re-run. Recover what did complete from the run's journal.jsonl (per-agent result rows survive the failure) rather than re-running from scratch, then hand-verify the top candidates. Second lesson from the same incident: when hand-verifying an OPA finding, 'opa eval -i file' takes the file AS the input document — wrapping it in {"input": …} makes every field undefined and the policy evaluates FALSE, manufacturing a false refutation of a real fail-open. Debug by evaluating sub-expressions (data.<pkg>.verb, the helper call) — all-undefined means the input shape is wrong, not that the finding is.
